A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEUBAY research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original bandit experiments, evaluations on 33 D4RL/NeoRL datasets, ablations, model-error analyses and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds fixed-horizon and SAC-backbone ablation results in Tables 14–15.

M1.justification: The proposed algorithm retains its frozen model ensemble, LayerNorm, adaptive uncertainty truncation, recurrent actor–critic and REDQ loss. Fixed horizons and SAC are evaluated as ablations, rather than adopted as changes to the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same bandit scenarios and 33 datasets spanning D4RL locomotion, NeoRL locomotion, Adroit and AntMaze. The new ablations change algorithm configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ROMI to Tables 10–12 and adds RAMBO and COMBO specifically to the AntMaze comparison in Table 12, although both appeared elsewhere in v2. The separate MOPO/Unifloral runtime comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: New controls use fixed horizons H=3, 10 and 256, replacing 256 with 32 for Adroit, and evaluate SAC with uncertainty quantiles 1.0 and 0.9. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets and termination handling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 14 adds direct adaptive-versus-fixed horizon tests across 28 datasets. Table 15 tests whether the horizon finding depends on REDQ by substituting SAC on 12 locomotion datasets. These substantially strengthen controls on the central mechanism; existing memory, LayerNorm and AntMaze failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Benchmark reporting retains six seeds, 20 evaluation episodes or 100 for AntMaze, standard deviations and one-sided Welch tests at p<0.05. Percentile-band practices are also unchanged. New ablation tables follow the existing point-estimate format without introducing new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial controlled results and comparator scores. For walker2d-medium-v2, Table 14 reports 106.4 with adaptive horizons versus 60.2, 4.5 and 2.4 at fixed H=256, 10 and 3. Table 15 adds SAC scores of 80.2 at quantile 1.0 and 0.9 at quantile 0.9. Some runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, LayerNorm bound, bootstrapped-error analysis, concentrability definitions, propositions, theorem and supporting proofs are retained. Appendix regrouping and equation renumbering do not substantively alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The headline claim is qualified to 'without explicit conservatism,' expressly excluding generic online anti-overestimation mechanisms. The central Bayesian formulation, long-horizon contribution and seven-dataset state-of-the-art claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges REDQ's possible mild underestimation and interprets it as secondary stabilization relative to horizon length. Section 6 explicitly discusses permission for test-time adaptation, safety-oriented penalties and the limitation of selecting hyperparameters using the true environment.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly discloses true-environment performance-based hyperparameter selection and widens the recommended real-data ratio range from [0.5,0.8] to [0.5,0.95]. It removes Markov-agent runtime/memory figures and the JAX optimization discussion. These are documentation changes; the main experimental hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds deployment-adaptation comparisons with Hong et al. and Swazinna et al., alongside ROMI and additional application references, and removes the Unifloral discussion. Most research positioning is retained; ADM-v2 and BA-MCTS publication updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract and main narrative is condensed or rewritten. Appendices are reorganized, the Markov-ablation discussion and reproducibility statement move, and the LLM-use appendix disappears. A previously valid Zhang et al. citation becomes malformed in Appendix B.1.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column preprint formatting to a two-column conference layout. Figures are resized and relocated, learning-curve panels are regrouped across Figures 6–9, captions and legends change, Tables 10–12 gain columns, and Tables 14–15 are added.

improvement.justification: Tables 14–15 provide useful direct controls for adaptive horizons and backbone dependence, while the qualified conservatism claim and explicit tuning disclosure improve transparency. These gains extend an already substantial empirical study. They outweigh the loss of some compute detail and the malformed citation, supporting a limited overall improvement.
